I am 70 years old. I went to primary school only, but I have been in the field for 60 years. My hands know this land better than any book. I have 16.9 mu, all wheat and maize, one after the other like everyone else in our village.

Let me think about this year the way I always do — look at what I did last year, look at what my neighbors are doing, and decide.

**My wheat (winter wheat):**
I already planted it last autumn, around early October. I used the improved variety the dealer sells — Jimai type, same seed my neighbor Old Wang uses. He gets good harvest every year, so I trust it. I sowed about 15 kg per mu, a bit heavy because my land is not the best and some seeds don't come up.

For fertilizer at sowing, I put down compound fertilizer, 50 kg per mu — this is the 15-15-15 bag. That gives me about 7.5 kg each of N, P, K per mu at base. Then at spring green-up, around March, I top-dress with urea, one bag (about 25 kg) for every 2 mu — so about 12-13 kg urea per mu. Urea is 46% nitrogen, so that adds about 6 kg N per mu. Total N around 13-14 kg per mu. My neighbors do similar.

Irrigation: I have well water. Wheat needs water at green-up (spring), at jointing, and at grain filling. So 3 times. If spring is dry I may add one more. Let me plan 3.

Pesticide: I spray once for aphids in spring, once for weeds earlier. Maybe 2 times total. If rust shows up I add one more, but usually 2 is enough.

Tillage: after maize harvest I use rotary tiller — the machine guy comes to the village. Everyone does rotary now, nobody ploughs deep anymore.

Yield: last year I got about 450 kg per mu. I hope for 480 this year if weather is good.

**My maize (summer maize):**
After wheat harvest in June, I plant maize right away — no-till, I just drill the seed into the wheat stubble. This is what everyone does now. Saves time, saves money on tillage.

Seed: hybrid maize, Zhengdan or Xianyu type. About 2 kg per mu, around 4500 plants per mu.

Fertilizer: I use compound fertilizer at sowing, 40 kg per mu of 15-15-15, and then urea top-dress at big trumpet stage, about 20 kg urea per mu. So N total around 6 + 9 = 15 kg. P and K about 6 kg each.

Wait — for maize I think I use a bit more nitrogen than wheat because maize grows fast in summer and needs it. Let me say 18 kg N per mu total. My son-in-law told me maize likes nitrogen.

Irrigation: summer has some rain, but last few years been dry. I water 2 times usually — once after sowing if dry, once at tasseling. Sometimes 3 if no rain.

Pesticide: once for corn borer, maybe once for armyworm if I see them. 2 times.

Tillage: no-till direct seeding after wheat. That is the common way now.

Yield: maize usually gives me 550-600 kg per mu. I'll say 580.

Now let me write the JSON.
</br>

I am a careful old man. I don't like to waste money but I also don't want my harvest to fail. So I fertilize a bit on the generous side — better spend 20 yuan extra than lose 100 yuan of grain. My 3-person household depends on this land.
